DEEPAK GUPTA, J. (ORAL)
CM-24090-CII-2025 : This application has been filed under Order XLI Rule 19 of the Code of Civil Procedure, seeking recall of the order dated 26.11.2025, whereby the main appeal FAO-3310-2001 was dismissed in default for want of prosecution.
Issue notice of the application.
Mr. Neeraj Khanna, learned counsel appearing through VC on behalf of respondent No. 3-Insurance Company, submits that he has no objection to the allowing of the present application.
In view of the reasons stated in the application, coupled with the fact that the counsel for the Insurance Company raises no objection, the application is allowed.
The order dated 26.11.2025 is recalled.

As a result, the main appeal FAO-3310-2001 stands restored to its original number and is taken on Board for hearing today itself.
FAO-3310-2001 : Learned counsel for the parties submit that they are ready to address arguments on the merits of the appeal.

1 of 3 FAO-3310-2001 Joginder Vs. Ranbir 05.12.2025 2025:PHHC:169945 2. Heard.
3. The accident in question took place on 23.01.1998, when the appellant sustained multiple injuries due to the rash and negligent driving of Maruti Car No. DNH-7821.

In the claim petition filed under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, the learned Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, vide award dated 07.02.2001, awarded a sum of 1,50,000/-, payable jointly and severally by the driver, owner,
Joginder Singh vs Ranbir Singh on 5 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/70551318/
1 and insurer of the offending vehicle, along with interest.

4. The Tribunal awarded compensation under the following heads:
 Head of Compensation Amount
Mental shock, pain & sufferings

10,000/-
  Medical expenses  53,000/-
  Conveyance  7,000/-
  Attendant charges  10,000/-
  Loss of income  20,000/-
  45% permanent disability,
  50,000/-
 loss of comforts, future enjoyment
Seeking enhancement, learned counsel for the appellant submits that the appellant was 34 years old at the time of accident and had sustained multiple grievous injuries.
As per medical evidence, he suffered fractures of both bones of the right leg, requiring major surgical interventions--including nailing, screw fixation and subsequent bone grafting.
He remained hospitalized from 23.01.1998 to 26.03.1998.
The sustained injuries resulted in 45% permanent disability.

6. It is argued that despite clear medical evidence indicating severe functional disability, the Tribunal awarded only 50,000/- under the composite head of disability, loss of comforts and loss of future enjoyment.

Learned counsel further submits that the minimum wages for an unskilled 2 of 3 FAO-3310-2001 Joginder Vs. Ranbir 05.12.2025 2025:PHHC:169945 worker in 1998 were approximately 1500/- per month, and therefore the compensation for permanent disability ought to have been computed on the basis of loss of future earning capacity, which the Tribunal failed to do.
7. Learned counsel for the Insurance Company is unable to refute the factual assertions or medical findings relied upon by the appellant, which indeed appear to be borne out from the record.

8. Upon deliberation, learned counsel for the Insurance Company, on instructions, agrees to pay 1,50,000/- as enhanced compensation, over and above the amount awarded by the Tribunal, to bring the compensation closer to what may be considered "just compensation" under Section 168 of the Motor Vehicles Act.

9. Consequently, and in view of the consensus reached between the parties, the present appeal is disposed of with the direction that the appellant shall be entitled to:
Joginder Singh vs Ranbir Singh on 5 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/70551318/
2  the original compensation awarded by the Tribunal; and  enhanced compensation of 1,50,000/-,  both amounts to be paid along with interest @ 7.5% per annum from the date of filing of the claim petition until actual realization.
Disposed of accordingly.
(DEEPAK GUPTA)
05.12.2025 JUDGE Vivek
